binders: Ω is a type equipped with a measurable-space structure.
μ is a measure on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance.
X : Nat → Ω → Real is a sequence of real-valued functions.
hypotheses: For every natural index i, X_i belongs to L2(μ), formalized as MeasureTheory.MemLp (X i) 2 μ.
For every pair of distinct natural indices i and j, X_i and X_j are independent under μ, formalized through ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (X i) (X j) μ.
For every natural index i, X_i and X_0 are identically distributed under μ, formalized as ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ.
conclusions: Along N → ∞ in Nat, the function N ↦ ∫ ω, |((N+1 : Real)⁻¹ · ∑_{i : Fin (N+1)} X_{i.val}(ω)) - ∫ ω, X_0(ω) ∂μ| ∂μ is Big-O of N ↦ 1 / sqrt((N+1 : Real)).
Equivalently, there exist constants C ≥ 0 and N₀ such that for every N ≥ N₀, the expected absolute deviation of the average of X_0,...,X_N from the integral of X_0 is at most C / sqrt(N+1).
mathematical_definitions: For N ∈ Nat, define the positive sample size n = N+1.
Define the empirical mean A_N(ω) = (1/(N+1)) ∑_{i=0}^{N} X_i(ω); Fin (N+1) ensures that the sum contains exactly N+1 terms.
Define the common center m = ∫ X_0 dμ. Identical distribution makes this the common expectation of the X_i.
Define the expected absolute error e_N = ∫ |A_N - m| dμ.
The conclusion e_N = O((N+1)^(-1/2)) means an eventual one-sided upper estimate: e_N ≤ C/(sqrt(N+1)) for some fixed C and all sufficiently large N.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Let X_0, X_1, ... be pairwise independent, identically distributed, square-integrable real random variables on a probability space. If the empirical average is formed from the first N+1 variables, then its expected absolute distance from the common mean is bounded, for all sufficiently large N, by a constant times 1/sqrt(N+1).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The independence assumption is pairwise: it is supplied separately for each distinct pair through IndepFun and does not state mutual or joint independence of every finite subfamily.
The indexing is deliberately shifted: parameter N corresponds to sample size N+1, and Fin (N+1) indexes exactly 0,...,N. Thus the denominator is never zero.
The centered value is specifically the integral of X_0, not an independently introduced mean parameter.
The outer integral is the expectation of the absolute pointwise error, not the absolute value of the bias.
MemLp at exponent 2 includes almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 norm; it is stronger than a bare finite-second-moment phrase without measurability.
IdentDistrib is asserted relative to μ on both source spaces and compares each X_i directly with X_0.
Big-O at Filter.atTop ignores finitely many initial N and allows the bounding constant to depend on μ and the sequence X, but not on N.
The Big-O claim is only an eventual upper bound. It does not assert an optimal constant, a matching lower bound, Θ behavior, or asymptotic equality.
Because the comparison function 1/sqrt(N+1) is positive and atTop on Nat is nontrivial, the conclusion is not made vacuous by division by zero or by an empty asymptotic regime.
No variance value or explicit bound such as sqrt(Var(X_0)) is included in the conclusion; all such scale information is absorbed into the unspecified Big-O constant.
ambiguities: The opaque wrapper in the elaborated body of IsBigO suppresses the explicit constant and threshold, but its standard semantic role here is the eventual norm upper bound stated in the translation.
The target uses Bochner integrals of real-valued functions; statements about values are consequently insensitive to changes on μ-null sets.

The proposition does not expose the measurable components bundled into or accompanying IdentDistrib and IndepFun beyond their declared interfaces, so the translation records their probabilistic meaning without strengthening them to joint independence.
